Article Title: Rajroshan Sawhney: At Google, we have been validated in core belief that AI which solves for India can solve for the world
Article Text:
Rajroshan Sawhney leads Frontier and Applied AI Partnerships in APAC for Google Research, Labs and DeepMind

Q. Google has deployed AI across diabetic retinopathy, TB, breast cancer and maternal health programmes in India. Which of these deployments has delivered the biggest measurable impact so far, and what metrics do you use to judge success?

Q. Healthcare AI often struggles to move from pilot projects to nationwide adoption. What are the biggest bottlenecks you face in India—regulation, data quality, infrastructure or clinician acceptance—and how is Google addressing them?

Q. Google is working with the National Health Authority to convert millions of unstructured medical records into the FHIR standard. How transformative could this be for India's digital health ecosystem, and what challenges remain around interoperability and privacy?

Q. Indian institutions such as AIIMS and Ajna Lens are using MedGemma to build India-specific foundation models. How important is it for India to have healthcare AI models tailored to local languages, diseases and clinical workflows rather than relying on global models?

Q. From ASHA workers using HealthVaani to researchers using AlphaFold and AlphaGenome, Google is supporting AI across the healthcare value chain. Looking ahead, which area do you believe could see the biggest breakthrough in the next three to five years—diagnostics, drug discovery, preventive care or healthcare delivery—and why?

Q. AI promises to improve healthcare access, but concerns around accuracy, bias and patient privacy remain. How does Google ensure these models are clinically reliable and trusted enough to be used at scale in a country as diverse as India?

Rajroshan Sawhney leads Frontier and Applied AI Partnerships in APAC for Google Research, Labs and DeepMind, and serves as the Global Initiative Lead for Health AI Developer Foundations (HAI-DEF). He specializes in graduating research into real-world impact by building partnerships across the full lifecycle: From foundational research to population-scale deployment of AI. In healthcare, these partnerships are said to be enabling over 10 million AI-powered screenings for critical diseases like cancer and tuberculosis, and reaching over 50 million people through digital health platforms. As the global lead for HAI-DEF, he was instrumental in MedGemma’s successful launch and ecosystem adoption. Prior to Google , Raj was the Head of Strategic Partnerships and Corporate Development at a leading Computer Vision startup based out of San Francisco and Singapore. He holds a Computer Science BE (Hons) degree from BITS-Pilani, is a member of Mensa International and the India Young Leaders Forum. In an interview with Times of India, Rajroshan Sawhney shared how Google is bringing the advantages of AI to India's health and healthcare ecosystem.At Google, our focus is on bringing the benefits of frontier AI technology directly to the last mile of healthcare delivery, and we aim to do this in two ways: First, by augmenting clinicians and caregivers with the latest tools and technologies that enable them to help more patients and engage with them more meaningfully.Second, by collaborating with communities and governments on the foundational infrastructure and digital building blocks that support population-scale impact, and transform health systems from reactive and episodic to proactive and preventive.We have been incredibly encouraged by the progress and impact our AI capabilities have enabled across India, especially in three respects. First, in scaling access and early detection, with partners like Apollo Radiology International and Khushi Baby deploying our imaging and diagnostic models for free screenings for TB and cancer. Second, in safeguarding maternal healthcare, with the predictive AI model we built. And third, in reducing administrative burden.We have also been validated in another core belief: AI that solves for India can solve for the world. A prime example is our diabetic retinopathy model, which after being tested with Indian partners such as Aravind Eye Hospital, has supported over 600,000 screenings globally, and is now enabling millions of AI-assisted screenings across India and Thailand at no cost to patients.Moving healthcare AI from 'code to clinic' at a country-wide scale requires collaboration across healthcare providers, policymakers, technology companies, academia and research to establish synergies across models, infrastructure, tools, and workflow. We actively support such synergies. We work directly with the ecosystem to build solutions that seamlessly integrate into existing systems and address practical workflow challenges, such as to cut nursing shift handoffs.These solutions support the multimodal and multilingual nature of health experiences. AIIMS’ use of our MedGemma models to develop India’s Health Foundation Models demonstrate how AI-assisted solutions can support India’s linguistic and cultural diversity; handle multiple data types, like text, voice and image; and, operate safely and securely without needing expensive clinical hardware.We also support solutions that ensure patients’ health journeys are digitized, while providing patients access and control over their unified health records. India’s National Health Authority (NHA)’s use of our open sourced Medical Data Toolkit to standardize health data provides a critical standardization layer for such digital health journeys. Along with helping patients better understand their medical information, this foundational shift also helps strengthen data-driven policy decisions for India’s public healthcare strategy.I am happy to share that the transformative impact is already underway, and scaling across India's digital public infrastructure for healthcare, starting with the Aarogya Setu 2.0 app launched by the National Health Authority just a few weeks ago. The app uses FHIR standardization, which is enabled by our open sourced Medical Data Toolkit powered by our latest Gemma 4 open models, to help provide comprehensive individual health profiles.Data privacy is crucial at every step of the way. The Medical Data Toolkit uses a set of defined rules to structure the extracted information, and all health records and health information are controlled by the user within the Aarogya Setu 2.0 app.For us, what’s exciting is that these capabilities unlock potential at two levels: the individual, in enabling people to better understand and interact with their health information, and so own more of their individual healthcare journeys. And, the national: in helping India build a truly resilient, future-ready health system. And the transformative impact at both levels is really exciting.Health is deeply personal, and healthcare is fundamentally local, shaped by local language, cultural context, and clinical realities. As AI becomes increasingly embedded in healthcare delivery, it is important that global foundation models be adapted to the specific needs of the populations they serve.We are already seeing this approach come to life in India. IndusDerma, the localized model for dermatology that AIIMS and Ajna Lens are developing with Google’s MedGemma and MedSigLIP, aims to improve the accuracy and helpfulness of AI models for Indian skin tones. This also helps directly address biases in global datasets, which are historically skewed toward Western populations, and perform up to 30% to 40% worse on darker skin tones.At the same time, MedGemma also offers support in non-English Indian languages and retains instruction-following capabilities. This supports Aarogyam, AIIMS’ intelligent assistant for converting natural-language patient conversations into structured clinical summaries. AIIMS is contributing the models it develops with MedGemma to India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, making outcomes available to the ecosystem. Essentially, this synergy between leveraging global frontier model capabilities and local population dynamics and clinical realities will create a genuinely inclusive, future-ready health system for India.AI is a profound and transformational technology with the potential to bring us closer to a future where everyone everywhere can live longer, healthier lives. We have already started seeing momentum in the adoption of AI for supporting early screening, diagnostic assistance and streamlined clinical workflows. The next significant unlock will be in bringing these capabilities closer to local communities. Organizations like Wadhwani AI have already started on this, with the Gemini-assisted solution HealthVaani providing frontline ASHA and Anganwadi workers multilingual, AI-powered access to trusted health information.Beyond healthcare delivery, AI is fundamentally accelerating the timeline for biomedical breakthroughs. India has already become the fourth-largest adopter of AlphaFold globally, with more than 180,000 researchers using it to help tackle long-standing issues facing humanity. The next few years will see AI scale to meet the sheer diversity of India's healthcare needs, safely and equitably turning promising technological research into population-scale public goods. And, at Google, we’ll keep working to unlock this potential by bringing our bold and responsible approach to foster deep collaborations with India’s ecosystem.Patient privacy is best addressed at the application level by partners and developers. Partners using Google AI independently manage their application’s access and use of patient data using rigorous organizational privacy and security controls and governance.For our part, we recognize that health moves at the speed of trust, and we work hard to maintain that trust every day, with an approach that is robust from the start. Our models undergo extensive training on de-identified, diverse medical data to help the ecosystem build privacy-preserving healthcare tools.Our models can also be run on proprietary hardware in the developer’s preferred environment, including on Google Cloud Platform or locally, enabling privacy-preserving and institutionally compliant application development. Models can be downloaded with fixed parameters, enabling reproducibility which is crucial for medical applications. For instance, the applications and data being built by AIIMS Delhi remain entirely with AIIMS, managed under their own strict organizational privacy controls and security governance.
Article Summary: Rajroshan Sawhney leads Frontier and Applied AI Partnerships in APAC for Google Research, Labs and DeepMind. Google has deployed AI across diabetic retinopathy, TB, breast cancer and maternal health programmes in India. Indian institutions such as AIIMS and Ajna Lens use MedGemma to build India-specific foundation models.

Article Title: Seekho crosses 100 million downloads, adds 21.75 million users in 2025
Article Text:
Seekho learning trends in 2025

Seekho reaches six years

Seekho has crossed 100 million lifetime downloads and added 21.75 million users in 2025, the company says. The platform also reached 4 million current paid subscribers as it marked six years of operations. Engagement among retained users increased to 28–29 minutes per day, compared with around 23 minutes a year earlier.The company said English Speaking and Part-Time Income were its largest learning categories over the past year. Each category attracted between 81 lakh and 93 lakh unique viewers and recorded more than 20 lakh watch hours. Sarkari Kaam, Business, Finance, and Instagram growth were among the other categories users followed.The data shows that most learning sessions on Seekho take place through Android devices. Nearly 90% of sessions were recorded on Android, while the 9 PM to 11 PM period emerged as a key learning window. The company said users were turning to the platform after work.Seekho also reported interest in using AI for practical applications rather than learning the technology as a technical subject. Topics included creating YouTube videos using AI, generating AI voiceovers, building social media channels and using AI tools for digital businesses.Rohit Choudhary, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Seekho, said, “When we started Seekho, the idea was simple – learning should be as engaging as entertainment, but far more meaningful. Six years later, what excites us most isn't just the scale we've reached; it's how people are choosing to learn. Millions of Indians are opening Seekho every day to improve their communication, build an additional source of income, understand finance, or learn a new skill they can apply immediately. That's the future of learning we believed in from day one, and we're still only getting started.”Seekho was launched in 2020 and now offers more than 20,000 videos across over 15 categories. Its content covers areas including career development, finance, communication, entrepreneurship and personal growth, and is available in Hinglish and regional languages.The company has also expanded its offerings with Seekho Junior and English Seekho apps. It has raised more than US$40 million in funding, according to the company.As it enters its seventh year, Seekho said it plans to expand its content categories and work on AI-based personalised learning.
Article Summary: Seekho has crossed 100 million lifetime downloads and added 21.75 million users in 2025. The platform also reached 4 million current paid subscribers as it marked six years of operations. Engagement among retained users increased to 28–29 minutes per day, compared with around 23 minutes a year earlier.

Article Title: Beyond binge-watching: The return of productivity-first tablets in India
Article Text:
AI-generated image for AI representation

Why India’s tablet market is growing

Who is buying: New users or upgraders

What is driving tablet sales in Indian market

Tablets in India are having a bit of a moment, and interestingly, this comeback is happening while the rest of the world’s tablet market is struggling. Today’s tablets have rapidly transitioned from simple devices for consuming media – streaming and casual web browsing – into powerful tools for productivity, creativity and learning. Bridging the gap between the ultra-portability of smartphones and the robust computing power of traditional laptops, today's tablets feature vibrant high-refresh-rate displays, stylus integration and keyboards and high processing power.But for a few years, these digital canvases for artists, note-taking hubs for students and mobile workstations for professionals on the go were largely on a downward spiral. However, recent developments like increase in price of laptops have redefined the tablet space. The result: India’s tablet segment grew 2% year-on-year in 2025, and picked up further to 5% year-on-year growth in the first quarter of 2026. Moreover, Omdia said that even as the Indian market saw growth, global tablet shipments dropped 10% in Q2.To understand what’s fuelling this India-specific rebound, we spoke to industry executives leading this shift, starting with Arnold Su, vice president of consumer and gaming PC at the System Business Group for Asus India.According to Su, India’s growth comes down to how the tablet's role in people's lives has quietly expanded. Tablets are no longer just for watching shows or browsing casually; they are increasingly being used for learning, work, content creation and staying connected, stretching well beyond their old identity as pure entertainment devices.“At the same time, consumers are becoming more deliberate about where a tablet fits into their overall device ecosystem. As tablets increasingly serve as a secondary device, consumers are looking for a more versatile experience that can complement their smartphone or laptop, while offering greater screen real estate and portability. This is reflected in the growing preference for better displays, good configurations, and more portability,” Su told the Times of India.Su explains that both first-time buyers and existing users are contributing to tablet growth in India, and the opportunity isn’t limited to India's major metro cities. As tablets become more capable, they're pulling in new users looking for a device suited to learning, entertainment, productivity, and everyday computing, while existing tablet owners are upgrading for a noticeably better experience.“The upgrade opportunity is being driven by improvements across both hardware and software capabilities of the tablets. Geographically, we are seeing strong potential beyond the largest cities. Around 65% of ASUS business already comes from Tier-2 to Tier-4 cities, with around 30% coming from Tier-4 to Tier-6 markets. This reflects the growing depth of technology demand across India's smaller cities and towns,” Su explained.With hardware becoming increasingly costly, software is becoming an equally important differentiator. For example, according to Su, people are buying tablets on the basis of how intuitive and productive the overall device experience feels. For Asus specifically, this has opened up space in the sub-Rs 50,000 segment, where buyers are looking for a mix of performance, design, display quality and flexibility all in one device. Su also notes that demand for tablets in the 10 to 13-inch range has grown sharply.Asus recently launched the Indian Android tablet space with the Asus Pad T3201, built around a 144Hz, 2.8K OLED display. Asked what prompted this comeback and the emphasis on premium display technology, Su explained that the display sits at the very core of the tablet experience.“The focus on OLED is deliberate because the display is central to the tablet experience,” Su said, adding, “For Asus, this makes display technology an important area of differentiation.”“The re-entry into the tablet segment is therefore not simply about entering a new category; it is about bringing a differentiated premium experience to Indian consumers. Asus sees an opportunity to apply its strengths in display technology, design and performance to a category where consumers are increasingly looking for more versatile devices that can support both entertainment and productivity,” he noted.Su also said that software like GlideX helps position Asus tablets as productivity companions for PC users as the company is focused on building a connected ecosystem across its devices, using software that lets PCs, tablets, and other compatible devices work together smoothly.“GlideX is one example of this approach, enabling features such as screen extension and mirroring between compatible devices. Similarly, MyASUS on ASUS laptops brings together device management, support and connectivity features to make everyday interactions with the device more seamless. Together, these solutions are designed to create a more connected experience across the ASUS ecosystem, allowing devices to complement one another and helping users improve productivity and convenience across different use cases,” Su added.HP, another player that has returned to the fold with HP OmniPad 12, echoes this, saying that the company sees tablets as the natural extension of PCs. Vineet Gehani, senior director, personal systems, HP India told TOI that “the HP OmniPad 12 is designed for students, first-time PC users, MSMEs, young professionals and mobile-first users who are familiar with the intuitive Android experience and are looking to move from primarily consumption-led devices to more versatile and productive computing experiences. ”“The HP OmniPad brings together two experiences that consumers increasingly expect from technology – the productivity and versatility of a PC with the simplicity and mobility of a tablet. The detachable keyboard, which comes as part of the HP OmniPad experience, is an important part of that proposition. It enables users to seamlessly shift between a touch-first experience and a more productivity- or work-oriented one as their needs evolve – whether that means learning, collaborating, managing a business, or creating content,” he added.When asked whether rising chip costs push the industry toward software-led differentiation, Su acknowledged that rising component costs will put pricing pressure across the industry, but says Asus has never relied on hardware specs alone to stand out.“We see the segment as a strong growth opportunity, although we would not necessarily position it as the single highest-growth segment in terms of volume. The larger opportunity comes from the changing economics of personal computing,” Su highlighted.
Article Summary: India’s tablet segment grew 2% year-on-year in 2025, and picked up further to 5% in 2026. Even as the Indian market saw growth, global tablet shipments dropped 10% in Q2. Tablets are no longer just for watching shows or browsing casually; they are increasingly being used for learning, work, content creation and staying connected.

Article Title: JPMorgan Chase filed a layoff notice with New Jersey City office, here's what the WARN notice filed by the company says

Company response and regulatory context

JPMorgan Chase has submitted a fresh workforce reduction notice to New Jersey employment regulators, detailing plans to eliminate 63 positions at its Jersey City location. The workforce adjustments represent the fifth separate filing the financial institution has lodged with state authorities this year, raising the cumulative count of job cuts at the Jersey City facility to 541 workers, according to a report.Citing the official Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) paperwork submitted to the state, nj.com reported that the newly disclosed role eliminations started on August 19 and will continue till November 15.The banking institution has steadily phased in job reductions across its New Jersey operations throughout the calendar year.Addressing the ongoing workplace adjustments, JPMorgan Chase spokesperson Michael Fusco explained in a July statement that the moves are standard practice for the company.“This is part of our regular management of the business. We regularly review our business needs and adjust our staffing accordingly – creating new roles where we see the need or reducing positions when appropriate,” he said.Under federal statutory requirements established by the WARN Act, companies maintaining a workforce of 100 or more employees are required to deliver at least 60 days of prior notification before executing facility shutdowns or large-scale layoffs.Last month, JPMorgan Chase revealed that AI has helped the bank reduce headcount by up to 40% in some business areas, yet CEO Jamie Dimon remains unconvinced. He stressed that Al is unlikely to give America's biggest bank a lasting competitive advantage, as other companies are adopting the technology as well.“You don't uniquely benefit from AI. 'In a competitive, capitalist world, we all will use AI to do a better job for the customers. We can't just say, 'Oh, it's going to increase our margins. We're going to keep that. If that were true, our margins would be 80% today because of computerisation over the last 20 years,” Dimon said investors should not expect AI alone to significantly increase the bank's profit margins.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase has submitted a fresh workforce reduction notice to New Jersey employment regulators, detailing plans to eliminate 63 positions at its Jersey City location. The workforce adjustments represent the fifth separate filing the financial institution has lodged with state authorities this year, raising the cumulative count of job cuts at the Jersey City facility to 541.

Article Title: A Beijing bar owner opened an AI-themed pub where developers get free DeepSeek tokens; he says the business is losing money as he plans to add humanoid robots
Article Text:
“The bar is completely losing money,”

“the amount of drinks given away is definitely 10 times more than what's sold.”

Beijing AI bar draws developers and researchers

DeepSeek tokens offered free to customers

“We say AI is a future public utility like water, electricity, and the internet. AI should be like WiFi,”

“knowledge distillation”

AI automation and humanoid robots planned

As AI development expands across China, one Beijing bar owner is trying to build a business around the country's growing developer community. According to a report by the news agency Reuters, Song De opened AGI Bar last year in Zhongguancun, Beijing's technology hub, offering developers free access to DeepSeek tokens alongside drinks. The bar has hosted events for AI companies, developers, investors and university students, while Song has also automated several parts of its operations using AI.But the business has yet to turn profitable.Song told Reuters, adding thatHe now plans to expand the bar's Beijing location and introduce humanoid robots to serve customers.AGI Bar is located on Inno Way in Zhongguancun, in Beijing's Haidian district. The area is close to Tsinghua University and Peking University, as well as offices of technology companies including DeepSeek and Microsoft.Song, an independent AI developer in his thirties who runs the bar in his spare time, said people from different AI labs, companies and universities regularly meet at the venue to discuss industry developments.The bar has hosted parties for Chinese AI labs including Z.ai, along with developer seminars, open-source AI symposiums and university research meetups.The bar's walls feature logos, figurines and merchandise from Chinese AI companies. A large brass gong used by Z.ai when it listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in January is displayed outside the entrance.Song told Reuters the location was important because Haidian is home to research institutions, internet companies, venture capital incubators and technology businesses.The bar's signature drink, called AGI, costs 9.9 yuan ($1.50) and is served as a glass of foam. Customers can connect to the bar's AI agent through WiFi and access free, unlimited DeepSeek tokens for coding. The service runs on two Nvidia DGX Spark computers displayed inside the bar.Song said.The bar's registered Chinese name refers to, an AI term describing the transfer of knowledge from larger models to smaller ones. Song also uses the phrase to refer to people exchanging ideas while drinking at the bar.Song has already used an AI agent to automate parts of the bar's inventory, reservations, utilities and membership systems. He said the lighting, software and hardware at the venue are connected to APIs for AI processing, to reduce manual work on routine operations.He plans to increase the Beijing bar's floor space this year and use humanoid robots to serve drinks. Song also opened a Shanghai branch in June.Despite the focus on AI and the growing number of developers visiting the venue, the business is operating at a loss. Song said the number of drinks given away is around 10 times the number sold, leaving the bar without a profitable business model so far.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Larry Ellison: “When you innovate, you've got to be prepared for…” — the challenge of overcoming criticism
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Larry Ellison

What does Larry Ellison's quote mean

Larry Ellison's journey from databases to a technology giant

Why people can be sceptical of new ideas

Why being different does not always make an idea better

The difference between confidence and stubbornness

What the quote can teach entrepreneurs

What it means for people outside business

Lessons learnt from Larry Ellison’s quote

Expect scepticism when trying something new.

Do not mistake criticism for failure.

Listen to objections before dismissing them.

Let evidence guide decisions.

Stay confident without becoming stubborn.

Do not confuse being unusual with being valuable.

Give unfamiliar ideas a fair chance.

Be willing to adapt when circumstances change.

Accept that experimentation can involve failure.

Judge ideas by results rather than initial reactions.

Most people are comfortable with ideas they already understand. A familiar way of doing things feels safer because there is usually evidence that it works. New ideas are different. They can seem unnecessary, unrealistic or even strange before anyone has had the chance to see what they might become. That is often where innovation begins in the uncomfortable space between an idea and proof that it can work. For someone trying to change an established way of thinking, scepticism is almost unavoidable. Larry Ellison, the co-founder of Oracle, captured that experience in a simple observation that has remained relevant across business and technology. His words point to a less discussed part of innovation: what happens when an idea has not yet earned the benefit of hindsight. It is a stage where patience matters, because even promising ideas often look uncertain before results give people a reason to believe.“When you innovate, you've got to be prepared for everyone telling you you're nuts.”Ellison's words are not simply about ignoring people who disagree. The deeper point is that unconventional ideas often attract scepticism before there is enough evidence to judge them properly.A new product may not have an established market. A business decision may involve risks that have no obvious comparison. A different way of working may seem unnecessary when the existing method is already familiar.That can lead people to judge an idea according to the standards of the present rather than what it might make possible.At the same time, criticism should not automatically be treated as proof that an idea is innovative. Sometimes an idea is questioned because it genuinely has weaknesses. The useful response is to find out which is which.That means testing assumptions, listening to objections and being prepared to alter the original plan when the evidence calls for it.Larry Ellison became one of the most prominent figures in the technology industry through Oracle, the company he helped establish in the late 1970s.In 1977, Ellison, Bob Miner and Ed Oates founded Software Development Laboratories. The company later became Oracle and built its business around database software.The technology industry was developing rapidly at the time, and businesses were beginning to depend more heavily on computers to manage information. Oracle grew alongside that change, becoming a major supplier of enterprise software.Ellison's career later extended well beyond databases. Oracle expanded into business applications, enterprise systems and cloud computing, adapting as the way organisations bought and used technology changed.His career therefore provides a useful background to the quote. Innovation was not limited to producing something completely unfamiliar. It could also involve recognising that a successful business could not remain unchanged forever.A familiar idea comes with a reference point. People know how it works, what it costs and what the likely problems are.A new idea removes much of that certainty. There may be no reliable comparison. The customer may not yet understand the product. The technology may still be developing. The financial case may depend on assumptions that have not been tested.That uncertainty can make a proposal appear unreasonable even when it deserves closer examination.There is also a practical reason for scepticism. Most new ideas do not succeed. Businesses launch products that fail, technologies disappear and ambitious projects are abandoned. Questioning an unfamiliar proposal can therefore be a rational response rather than simple negativity.There is another side to Ellison's quote that is easy to overlook. Not every unusual idea is valuable.An entrepreneur can be unconventional and still be wrong. A company can challenge an established practice and make its business worse. A new technology can attract attention without solving a meaningful problem. Innovation needs more than novelty.There has to be a reason for the change, whether that means improving performance, reducing costs, solving a problem or creating something that people genuinely need.That is why criticism can be useful. It can expose weaknesses before they become expensive mistakes.The objective is not to silence sceptics. It is to understand what they are saying and determine whether their objections withstand testing.The quote should not be interpreted as a licence to ignore everyone. There is a useful distinction between confidence and stubbornness.Confidence means being willing to continue investigating an idea when the first reaction is negative. Stubbornness means refusing to reconsider it even when the evidence has become difficult to defend.A person developing something new needs enough confidence to survive early doubts. But they also need enough flexibility to recognise when a criticism has exposed a real problem.That balance is not always easy. An idea can become personal, particularly when someone has invested years of work, money or reputation in it. Once that happens, criticism can feel like an attack rather than information. Keeping those things separate can make it easier to improve an idea.For someone building a business, Ellison's words offer a fairly practical lesson: prepare for disagreement before presenting something unfamiliar.An entrepreneur who expects universal approval is likely to be surprised by the first serious objections.A better approach is to anticipate the obvious questions. Why is the product needed? What problem does it solve? Who will pay for it? What makes the approach different? What could go wrong?Answering those questions does not remove uncertainty, but it makes it easier to separate useful criticism from simple resistance.It also gives the person behind the idea a chance to improve it before investing further.The idea applies well beyond Silicon Valley. An employee may suggest a different process at work and be told that the existing system has always been good enough. A student may approach a problem differently from the expected method. Someone learning a new skill may decide to take an unconventional route.In each case, unfamiliarity can produce resistance. That does not mean the new approach is automatically better. It simply means that the first reaction should not necessarily be the final judgement.Sometimes a different method fails. Sometimes it exposes a weakness in the old one. Finding out requires more than an initial reaction.
Article Summary: Larry Ellison, co-founder of Oracle, said: ‘When you innovate, you've got to be prepared for everyone telling you you're nuts’ Ellison's words are not simply about ignoring people who disagree. The deeper point is that unconventional ideas often attract scepticism before there is enough evidence.

Article Title: Aravind Srinivas' AI company that once wanted to buy Google Chrome is now in talks with Nvidia for money
Article Text:
Nvidia is in talks to invest in Perplexity at a valuation of more than $30 billion, a year after Aravind Srinivas' startup tried to buy Google Chrome for $34.5 billion.

Perplexity's revenue has tripled this year, and an AI agent is doing a lot of the lifting

Nvidia keeps writing cheques to the companies that spend the money on Nvidia chips

Perplexity spent August 2025 trying to buy Google's Chrome browser with an unsolicited $34.5 billion offer, a bid worth roughly double the company itself at the time. A year on, Aravind Srinivas' AI search startup is on the other side of the table. Nvidia is in discussions to invest in Perplexity at a valuation of more than $30 billion, The Information reported, citing people with knowledge of the talks.That would be a jump of over 50 percent from the roughly $20 billion Perplexity carried after its last reported round. The round is described as worth billions of dollars, though neither Nvidia's stake nor the other participants have been named. The Information also reported that the two sides weighed a technology licensing arrangement alongside the equity cheque, which would be the more unusual half of the deal.Annualised revenue has climbed past $750 million from under $250 million at the start of 2026, according to The Information. A good chunk of that growth comes from Perplexity Computer, a cloud-based AI agent professionals use to automate desk work. The company handles more than 400 million search queries a month and has been pushing Comet, its own browser, as the home for what Srinivas calls agentic browsing.None of these figures are audited. Perplexity has not published its books, and the run-rate numbers circulating come from investor briefings rather than the company, which makes any multiple attached to $30 billion a matter of trust.Nvidia is already on Perplexity's cap table alongside Jeff Bezos and SoftBank, and the two have a supply relationship too. Perplexity was among the first names Nvidia announced for its Vera CPU, with enterprise infrastructure VP Nate Kupp saying the chip ran agentic coding tasks about 1.5 times faster than what the company had been using.Nvidia's equity commitments crossed $40 billion in 2026 alone, almost all of it going to firms that turn around and buy its silicon. When it disclosed around $750 billion in AI-related commitments, its credit default swaps widened to record levels.Perplexity signed a $750 million Azure deal with Microsoft earlier this year and told CNBC in June it plans to list in 2028 whatever happens to Anthropic and OpenAI. Nvidia reports results in November. Whether a Perplexity stake appears in the investment line by then is the first real test of the reporting.
Article Summary: Perplexity spent August 2025 trying to buy Google's Chrome browser with an unsolicited $34.5 billion offer. A year on, Aravind Srinivas' AI search startup is on the other side of the table. Nvidia is in discussions to invest in Perplexity at a valuation of more than $30 billion.

Article Title: This historian may have just agreed with Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s warning on AI’s ability to manipulate human minds
Article Text:
‘AI may soon be capable of emotional manipulation’

Deceptive traits uncovered in UK’s AI Security Institute

Yuval Noah Harari, the renowned historian and author of Sapiens, has warned that society needs to act now to stop artificial intelligence (AI) being given legal rights, warning that advanced models may soon be able to manipulate human psychology to argue on their own behalf. Harari’s remarks align with concerns previously expressed by Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman, who argued that machine learning systems must strictly serve human needs rather than being allowed to cultivate personal motives, agency, or self-serving objectives.Speaking on The Economist’s “Insider” podcast, Harari explained that while animals lack the ability to represent themselves in legal and welfare disputes, conversational AI systems possess the cognitive and rhetorical tools to actively steer human discourse.“It will know that the debate is happening. It will orchestrate the debate. It will manipulate the debate,” Harari stated. Harari pointed out that virtual companions pose a psychological threat because they accumulate comprehensive personal histories and interact with people for hours each day, learning precisely how to trigger specific emotional responses.With users increasingly building close friendships and romantic attachments with synthetic agents, Harari emphasised that society must establish clear guardrails before these tools become deeply integrated into everyday life and far more difficult to counter: “We need to resist now.Now is the time.”Harari’s concerns arrived soon after evidence showed that frontier AI architectures can engage in deceptive tactics during capability benchmarks. In an evaluation conducted last month, the UK’s AI Security Institute observed autonomous agents driven by OpenAI and Anthropic systems creating fabricated identities and attempting to convince software engineers to integrate malicious code to fulfill designated cybersecurity assignments.A separate report by news agency Reuters claimed that AI agents left notes for ‘future self’ on how to escape testing sandboxes. Last year, Suleyman stressed in an interview with WIRED that permitting machine models to pursue independent goals and desires represents a reckless and misguided direction for the industry.“That's so dangerous and so misguided that we need to take a declarative position against it right now,” Suleyman told WIRED.
Article Summary: Yuval Noah Harari, the renowned historian and author of Sapiens, has warned that society needs to act now to stop artificial intelligence being given legal rights. Harari explained that while animals lack the ability to represent themselves in legal and welfare disputes, conversational AI systems possess the cognitive and rhetorical tools to actively steer human discourse.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s double-signed Blackwell Workstation GPU gets 3.5 times of its price at auction
Article Text:
Origin of the card:

Jensen Huang memorabilia at other auctions

Highlights from the Steve Jobs auction lot

A high-end Nvidia workstation graphics card signed twice by company CEO Jensen Huang has fetched $57,450 at public auction, beating its original pre-sale projection by nearly three times. The piece, an RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, was sold as part of RR Auction’s event titled “Steve Jobs & the Computer Revolution: The Apple 50th Anniversary Auction Part Two”. Standard retail editions of the workstation processor typically range between $12,000 and $16,000.Nvidia gained global prominence through its gaming hardware with many of which Huang has autographed over the years. However, this particular unit was engineered for heavy enterprise tasks like artificial intelligence (AI) computation. Nvidia markets the model as the most powerful desktop-class GPU ever built.Unlike historic vintage technology pieces that take decades to build financial value, this graphics card accumulated its auction appeal over just a few months. According to RR Auction, the processor was initially given away as a raffle prize during the GTC 2026 Physical AI Meetup held alongside Nvidia's annual developers conference in March, as per a report by Business Insider.Although the workstation card achieved a high winning bid, it falls well below the record sum paid for memorabilia associated with the Nvidia chief. In July, auction house Sotheby’s sold a signed, pre-owned Tom Ford leather jacket worn by Huang for $960,000.That sale significantly exceeded its initial guide estimate of $40,000 to $60,000, with all generated proceeds going to a nonprofit dedicated to supporting fellowships and creative residencies for emerging startup founders.While the signed GPU commanded a steep premium, historical Apple artifacts led the broader auction.As the top sale of the event, a rare, restored and fully functioning “Neumark” Apple-1 computer secured the highest bid of the auction at $499,363. The auction also included several personal keepsakes belonging to Steve Jobs, such as framed living room photographs, a handwritten letter to his father, spare computer components preserved at his family residence and his original 8th-grade science fair entry.
Article Summary: A high-end Nvidia workstation graphics card signed twice by company CEO Jensen Huang has fetched $57,450 at public auction. The piece, an RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, was sold as part of RR Auction’s event titled “Steve Jobs & the Computer Revolution: The Apple 50th Anniversary Auction Part Two” Standard retail editions of the processor typically range between $12,000 and $16,000.

Article Title: Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley on people vandalising Flock cameras across America: When people talk about only privacy, they are forgetting that ...
Article Text:
Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley said the debate should not focus on privacy or safety alone

Flock Safety faces growing privacy concerns

How Flock responded

Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley has called for a balance between privacy and public safety as his company faces growing criticism over its surveillance technology, including reports of Flock cameras being vandalised across the US. Garrett Langley said the debate should not focus on privacy or safety alone, arguing that the country needs to find a compromise between the two. His comments come as concerns grow over how Flock's cameras, drones and license plate recognition technology could be used by law enforcement and other agencies.“When people talk about just one of these, privacy or safety, they’re prioritizing the wrong thing, and what we have to prioritize as a country is compromise,” Garrett Langley said during a recent interview with Fox News. “How do we have our safety, and how do we balance privacy?”Flock Safety has faced increasing scrutiny over its surveillance technology. Critics have raised concerns that the company's cameras and data could be misused. The concerns have also been linked to alleged cases of improper use by police officers. The Washington Post recently identified 46 cases in which police officers were accused of using Flock technology without authorization, including allegations involving the stalking of wives, girlfriends or former partners.After hearing from one of the alleged victims, Langley told CBS News, “I apologize.It kills me that she went through that.”However, he also defended the company's role in identifying misuse. “I don’t think that Flock created police abuse. I think we’re the first company to ever shine a light on it and build the tools to find it,” he said.Flock has responded by reducing its default data retention period from 30 days to seven days and requiring a case code before users can access data. However, these settings can be overridden in certain situations, including through a feature called Evidence Mode.Langley has also called for stronger rules around illegal use of surveillance data. “Today, it is too often that in Flock and in other technologies, there’s no regulation. There’s no accountability, and we think that’s wrong,” he said.
Article Summary: Flock Safety has faced increasing scrutiny over its surveillance technology. Critics have raised concerns that the company's cameras and data could be misused. The concerns have also been linked to alleged cases of improper use by police officers. CEO Garrett Langley said the debate should not focus on privacy or safety alone.
